title: Google Maps Popular Times & Traffic Analytics

searchQueries.title: Search queries
searchQueries.description: Venue types to collect, e.g. 'gym', 'cafe', 'shopping mall'. Each runs across the location below. A location is required with queries.

areaName.title: Location - named area
areaName.description: City, region or country, e.g. 'jakarta', 'bali', 'Austin, Texas'. Common cities use a built-in box; any other name is looked up on OpenStreetMap. For a precise area use a centre point with a radius, or a bounding box.

centerLatitude.title: Location - centre latitude
centerLatitude.description: Latitude of the centre point. Use with centre longitude and radius.

radiusKm.title: Location - radius (km)
radiusKm.description: Collect venues within this many kilometres of the centre point.

boundingBox.title: Location - bounding box [south, west, north, east]
boundingBox.description: Most precise option. Tiled into several search points, then filtered to the box using each venue's real coordinates.

tileSizeKm.title: Search tile size (km)
tileSizeKm.description: Spacing of search points inside your area. Smaller = more thorough, more requests. Leave empty to choose automatically.

maxPlacesPerQuery.title: Max places per query
maxPlacesPerQuery.description: Stop each query after this many venues. Each venue costs one extra request to fetch its popular-times curve.

placeUrls.title: Specific Google Maps URLs
placeUrls.description: Optional. Collect named venues directly instead of searching. Short links are followed automatically.

placeIds.title: Specific Place IDs / CIDs / feature IDs
placeIds.description: Optional. Accepts a Place ID (ChIJ...), a numeric CID, or a raw feature ID (0x...:0x...).

outputFormat.title: Output format
outputFormat.description: Wide keeps the whole weekly curve nested inside one row per venue. Long emits one row per venue/day/hour, which is what you want for CSV, spreadsheets and dataframes - group by hour across venues without unpacking anything.

onlyPlacesWithPopularTimes.title: Only keep venues that have popular times
onlyPlacesWithPopularTimes.description: Most small venues have no foot-traffic data at all. Leave on to keep the dataset to venues that do; switch off to also record which venues were checked and had none.

requestDelaySeconds.title: Delay between requests (seconds)
requestDelaySeconds.description: Pause between requests. Google returns less data to an IP that has made many recent requests, so slowing down can improve how many venues come back with a curve. Raise it for large runs.

exportFormats.title: Extra export files
exportFormats.description: Also write the results to the key-value store in these formats. The Apify dataset is always produced regardless.

language.title: Language (hl)
language.description: Google interface language. Affects busyness wording such as 'Usually a little busy'.

region.title: Region (gl)
region.description: Two-letter country code biasing Google's results, e.g. US, ID, GB.

proxyConfiguration.title: Proxy configuration
proxyConfiguration.description: Residential proxy is ON by default and this actor genuinely needs it. Google sends a reduced place record to datacenter IPs with the popular-times block stripped out entirely: measured on the Apify platform, the same run returned 0% coverage with no proxy and 62.5% coverage through RESIDENTIAL. Turning the proxy off will usually return no foot-traffic data at all. Note GOOGLE_SERP cannot be used here - it does not tunnel arbitrary HTTPS.
